issues.description: The manuscript gives mutually incompatible accounts of when the interventions occur. One passage says the warning is after collaborative recall, another says all resistance methods are before collaborative recall, while the procedure places them after collaborative recall. This is a critical design detail because a pre-exposure inoculation and a post-exposure warning test different mechanisms and have different causal interpretations.
issues.quote: “In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below).” / “What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).” / “The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation (and a control condition), and (4) an individual memory test of the original material.”

issues.description: The design section claims discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but the procedure states that every pair will discuss the same four critical details. This means discussed status is confounded with item identity, making it impossible to know whether differences reflect memory conformity or intrinsic differences in item memorability/salience.
issues.quote: “In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced.” / “In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.”

issues.description: Because the same critical details are always discussed, any observed difference between discussed and non-discussed items may be due to the particular items selected for discussion rather than misinformation. Critical details can differ substantially in baseline memorability, perceptual salience, distinctiveness, or ambiguity, so the central within-subject comparison is not internally valid without item counterbalancing or item-level modeling.
issues.quote: “In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric’s cap color and his company logo.”

issues.description: The manuscript alternately describes the final individual memory test as open-ended and as two-alternative forced choice. These formats produce different response processes, chance levels, scoring rules, and susceptibility estimates. The contradiction prevents evaluation or replication of the primary outcome.
issues.quote: “The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie, regardless of whether they were subsequently discussed.” / “In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.”

issues.description: The analysis plan first defines misinformation exposure based on what the partner actually said, but then states that all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation. These rules are incompatible. If a partner gives the participant’s correct answer, says “don’t know,” gives an unrelated answer, or no clear answer, treating the item as misinformation misclassifies exposure and biases the estimated memory conformity effect.
issues.quote: “In this case, each answer given by the partner of a participant that is inconsistent with what the participant was presented with is misleading.” / “In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events.”

issues.description: Participants are tested in interacting pairs and pairs are assigned to condition, but the proposed ANOVA appears to analyze individual participants as independent observations. Responses from members of the same dyad are statistically dependent because they share the same session, discussion, stimuli, intervention, and mutual influence. Ignoring dyadic clustering inflates precision, underestimates standard errors, and can increase Type I error.
issues.quote: “The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).” / “Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups” / “The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels”

issues.subcategory: item-level dependence and bounded outcomes ignored
issues.description: The planned ANOVA on participant-level counts ignores that responses are binary/categorical at the item level and bounded by a small number of critical items. It also ignores item variability, despite item identity being central to the design. A generalized mixed-effects model with random effects for dyad/participant and item, or an appropriately specified binomial model, would better match the data-generating process.
issues.quote: “Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers.” / “The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA”

issues.description: The power analysis is based on individual participant counts, but the experiment randomizes and treats participants in dyads. If there is intradyad correlation, the effective sample size is closer to the number of pairs than the number of individuals. The resulting power estimates are therefore likely optimistic, especially for between-condition comparisons.
issues.quote: “The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).” / “Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups” / “Considering the accessible financial, organizational and time resources, a sample of 240 participants was assumed”

issues.description: The replication power analysis uses a random-effects synthesis of only two highly discrepant effect sizes and then treats the resulting point estimate as stable. With only two studies and large heterogeneity, the uncertainty around the expected effect is substantial. This undermines the claim that a very small sample would suffice and weakens confidence in the power rationale.
issues.quote: “The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.”

issues.subcategory: directional tests unjustified by acknowledged bidirectional effects
issues.description: The manuscript plans directional significance tests, but it explicitly acknowledges that some interventions could increase suggestibility or memory conformity. When theoretically plausible effects exist in both directions, one-tailed/directional testing is not justified and can inflate false-positive conclusions for the predicted direction.
issues.quote: “Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.” / “If this is the case, increased memory conformity is possible.” / “Of course, demonstrating memory fallibility alone could have different results: it could even increase suggestibility”

issues.description: The analysis plan lists several outcome indices and accuracy summaries but does not specify a single primary outcome or correction strategy. Analyzing correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, total answers, filler accuracy, discussed accuracy, non-discussed accuracy, confidence, and DRM predictors creates substantial researcher degrees of freedom and multiplicity risk.
issues.quote: “We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.”

issues.subcategory: underspecified follow-up contrasts and multiplicity control
issues.description: The plan states that follow-up comparisons will be performed after a significant interaction, but it does not specify the exact contrasts, familywise error control, or whether planned comparisons versus control will be tested regardless of omnibus significance. This leaves flexibility in choosing comparisons and reporting significant results.
issues.quote: “In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.” / “Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.”

issues.subcategory: demand characteristics from explicit warning/deception disclosure
issues.description: Some interventions appear to tell participants directly that the partner may have been wrong, that the partner saw a different version, why deception was used, and that they should not rely on the partner. Any reduction in misinformation-consistent answers may therefore reflect demand compliance or response strategy rather than improved memory or reduced memory conformity.
issues.quote: “Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied” / “The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner.”

issues.subcategory: outcome cannot distinguish memory change from response strategy
issues.description: The operational definition of intervention efficacy is a smaller accuracy difference between discussed and non-discussed items. However, after explicit warnings and instructions, participants may simply adopt a response rule to distrust partner information. The design does not distinguish genuine memory preservation, source monitoring, demand compliance, or strategic withholding.
issues.quote: “The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if the magnitude of memory conformity (expressed as the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items) is smaller in the group in which this method was applied than in the control group.”

issues.description: The theoretical rationale depends on whether participants are aware of discrepancies between their own memory and the partner’s information, but the study does not include an item-level measure of discrepancy awareness or source memory before the final test. Without this, the key mechanism and predicted moderation cannot be tested, and null or positive effects will be difficult to interpret.
issues.quote: “Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.” / “Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.”

issues.subcategory: DRM task does not operationalize social influence
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation intervention uses a DRM false-memory task to demonstrate vulnerability to influence. DRM false recall of semantically associated lures primarily reflects associative memory processes, not interpersonal misinformation or co-witness conformity. The manipulation therefore may not validly instantiate the construct it is supposed to demonstrate.
issues.quote: “First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used”

issues.description: The manuscript asserts that normative influence is completely ruled out because the final test is individual. This is too strong. Normative pressures can operate during the collaborative recall itself, affect what is rehearsed or accepted, and persist through expectations about the partner or experimenter. Therefore the theoretical exclusion of normative influence is not warranted.
issues.quote: “Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.”

issues.description: The rationale imports inoculation theory from resistance to persuasion and illegitimate authority, but co-witness memory contamination is not necessarily a persuasive attack or unfair manipulation. The intervention may train participants to distrust a partner rather than inoculate against misinformation, limiting theoretical fit and interpretability.
issues.quote: “This was inspired by existing research on resisting social influence presented by Sagarin, Cialdini, Rice, & Serna (2002). Their technique was based on the inoculation theory” / “Afterwards, the participants will be motivated to resist illegitimate influences.”

issues.subcategory: interventions not matched for duration and cognitive load
issues.description: The intervention arms are not clearly matched for duration, interaction with the experimenter, cognitive effort, arousal, legal/emotional content, or retention interval before the final memory test. The DRM arm includes a memory task, feedback, and a motivational podcast, whereas other arms listen to podcasts. Differences in forgetting, fatigue, interference, attention, or motivation could confound treatment effects.
issues.quote: “The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast” / “The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast” / “First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used” / “Next, the participants’ motivation to resist memory suggestibility will consist in them listening to a podcast”

issues.subcategory: intervention components overlap and are not isolable
issues.description: The three interventions differ on multiple components and overlap substantially. Extended warning includes education and enlightenment; Education includes memory fallibility; Demonstration and motivation includes a memory fallibility demonstration plus motivation and direct instruction. Equal or different effects cannot be attributed to the named mechanisms without component controls.
issues.quote: “Secondly, we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation. Empirical results may help to determine to what extent the overlap is substantial; although, on the other hand, even if they produce the same results, this does mean that the mechanisms by which the were effective are always the same.”

issues.subcategory: control condition may not be inert
issues.description: The control podcast concerns soft skills and social attitudes, which could plausibly influence social conformity, confidence, cooperation, or attitudes toward the partner. It is therefore not a clearly neutral control for a memory conformity study.
issues.quote: “In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.”

issues.subcategory: response alternatives may themselves deliver misinformation
issues.description: During collaborative recall, participants see five possible responses. If these include both critical alternatives or plausible lures, the task itself supplies post-event misinformation independent of the co-witness. This confounds co-witness social influence with experimenter-provided recognition alternatives.
issues.quote: “Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer.”

issues.subcategory: retrieval practice confounded with misinformation exposure
issues.description: Discussed critical items receive collaborative retrieval practice and additional exposure, whereas non-discussed critical items do not. Differences between discussed and non-discussed items may therefore reflect retrieval practice, rehearsal, collaborative correction, or interference rather than misinformation alone, especially without counterbalancing or a no-misinformation discussion control.
issues.quote: “the participants will complete the collaborative recognition test. This is a series of questions, thanks to which the participants will discuss half of the discrepant details included in the original material, thus leading to mutual misinformation.”

issues.description: The manuscript does not provide a coding manual for classifying open-ended responses as correct, misinformation-consistent, other, or missing; does not state whether coders will be blind to condition; and does not specify interrater reliability or handling of ambiguous answers, synonyms, partial responses, or “don’t know.” This limits replicability and may introduce bias.
issues.quote: “Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers.”

issues.description: The discussion is audio recorded and both responses may be documented when agreement fails, but the manuscript does not specify how discussion content will be coded, how misinformation exposure will be determined from the audio, whether coders will be blind, or how disagreements and multiple answers will enter the analysis.
issues.quote: “If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented. The discussion will be audio recorded.”

issues.description: The experimenter administers condition-specific procedures and feedback, and open-ended outcomes require judgment. The manuscript does not mention blinding of experimenters, participants beyond the cover story, or outcome coders to condition and hypotheses. Lack of blinding can bias instructions, participant behavior, and scoring.
issues.quote: “At this moment in this group, the experimenter will give the following information to the participants” / “The discussion will be audio recorded.” / “Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test”

issues.description: The manuscript says pairs will be randomly assigned but does not describe the randomization method, allocation concealment, blocking/stratification, balancing by movie version, participant sex/gender, familiarity, experimenter, or session. Without these details, selection bias and imbalance cannot be assessed.
issues.quote: “Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups: (1) Extended warning, (2) Education about memory, (3) Demonstration and motivation, and (4) control condition.”

issues.subcategory: dyad familiarity and social variables uncontrolled
issues.description: Memory conformity is known to vary with relationship, familiarity, trust, dominance, and social dynamics. The study recruits participants through advertisements but does not specify whether dyad members are strangers, acquaintances, friends, or partners, nor whether these variables will be measured, constrained, or modeled.
issues.quote: “the participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.” / “the participants (always a pair of them) will watch the movie about Eric.”

issues.description: The task depends on visual perception of critical details, color discrimination, hearing podcasts/word lists, and understanding Polish materials, yet eligibility criteria are limited to age. The manuscript does not specify screening for color blindness, visual impairment beyond ordinary correction, hearing problems, language fluency, neurological/psychiatric conditions, or prior familiarity with the stimuli/paradigms.
issues.quote: “The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old” / “in the first version, Eric is trying on a black hat, whereas in the second version the hat is red” / “participants will listen to a podcast”

issues.description: The MORI technique depends on participants believing they saw the same film and not noticing image duality or glasses manipulation. The manuscript does not specify checks for suspicion, peeking, removal/tilting of glasses, cross-talk between images, or whether participants noticed their partner saw a different version before the intended warning.
issues.quote: “each of them sees a different movie version while being convinced that they are actually watching the same movie clip” / “Please make sure you watch the movie through the glasses (no peeking over the top or around the side)”

issues.description: The study does not specify checks that participants attended to, understood, or believed the podcasts; that the DRM manipulation actually induced false recall for a given participant; or that the motivational manipulation changed motivation. Without these checks, failed or heterogeneous manipulation uptake cannot be distinguished from ineffective interventions.
issues.quote: “The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast” / “The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast” / “The DRM procedure usually results in most of the participants falsely recalling at least a few of the critical lures.”

issues.description: The manuscript does not describe how missing item responses, incomplete confidence ratings, unusable audio, participant withdrawal, one member of a dyad being excluded, or partial technical failures will be handled. This is especially important because exclusions at the dyad level versus individual level affect independence and power.
issues.quote: “We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.”

issues.subcategory: exclusion criteria too narrow and underspecified
issues.description: Only technical problems are listed as exclusions. There are no prespecified rules for excluding participants who guess the purpose, notice the dual movie manipulation, fail to follow instructions, do not discuss, remove/peek over glasses, have language/hearing/vision problems, or provide unusable data. Post hoc decisions on these cases could bias results.
issues.quote: “We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.”

issues.description: The sample size is fixed at 240, but the manuscript does not state whether excluded participants or dyads will be replaced, whether recruitment stops at 240 enrolled or 240 analyzable participants, or how exclusions affect balance across conditions. This creates ambiguity in the final sample and power.
issues.quote: “The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).” / “We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.”

issues.subcategory: minor participant consent and ethics details missing
issues.description: The planned age range includes 16- and 17-year-old minors, and the study uses deception. The manuscript does not report consent/assent procedures, parental consent or waiver, ethics approval, or safeguards for deceptive procedures and debriefing with minors.
issues.quote: “The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old” / “In addition, the podcast will explain why the deception was applied.”

issues.description: The study uses self-selected 16–35-year-old participants recruited through media/internet advertisements, but the rationale invokes eyewitnesses and justice systems broadly. The manuscript does not adequately delimit generalization to older adults, children, actual crime witnesses, high-stress events, police interviews, or legally consequential settings.
issues.quote: “Due to the serious consequences of inaccurate testimonies, research on methods of reducing the memory conformity effect is extremely important for the proper functioning of justice systems.” / “The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.”

issues.description: The manuscript claims the MORI technique brings laboratory conditions closer to real-life witness discussions, but the planned event is a silent short film viewed through polarizing glasses, followed by structured recognition discussion with displayed options and laboratory interventions. These features differ substantially from real eyewitness contexts and limit ecological generalization.
issues.quote: “The main reason for its popularity is the fact that the MORI technique brings laboratory conditions closer to the real-life situations in which witnesses discuss a crime and are then individually interviewed by law enforcement officers.” / “the participants will watch a silent movie that lasts 6 minutes and 34 seconds”

issues.subcategory: mechanistic causal claims not supported by measurements
issues.description: The manuscript makes causal claims about interventions increasing alertness, source monitoring, discrepancy detection, reliance on own memory, and abandonment of the consistency assumption. None of these mediators is directly measured, so the study can at most estimate condition effects on responses, not establish the proposed causal mechanisms.
issues.quote: “To sum up, we assumed that the extended warning would cause participants to abandon the consistency assumption, make them more alert to discrepancies between their memories and information provided by the partner, and consequently cause them to rely on their own knowledge while completing the individual memory test.”

issues.subcategory: confidence measure not integrated into hypotheses or analysis
issues.description: Participants provide confidence ratings for every answer, and the theory repeatedly invokes confidence/lack of confidence as a mechanism. However, the analysis plan does not specify confirmatory analyses for confidence, calibration, or whether confidence mediates intervention effects. This is a missed construct-validity opportunity and leaves another flexible outcome.
issues.quote: “Moreover, for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty).”

issues.subcategory: stimulus and apparatus calibration details incomplete
issues.description: The MORI setup requires careful control of image alignment, luminance, polarization leakage, viewing angle, and visibility of critical details. The manuscript gives basic apparatus dimensions but does not report calibration procedures or validation that each participant sees only the intended version with equivalent quality.
issues.quote: “The movie will be projected with two LED projectors placed such that the two images overlap on the screen.” / “Polarizing filters will be placed in front of the lens of each projector: one will be oriented vertically and the other horizontally.”

issues.description: The collaborative recognition test is central to misinformation exposure, but the manuscript does not provide the 12 questions, the five alternatives, which four critical details are discussed, or how alternatives are ordered/counterbalanced. This prevents replication and evaluation of whether the questions introduce bias or differential difficulty.
issues.quote: “The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details (e.g., What color was Eric’s cap?), with the other eight being control questions. Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer.”

issues.description: The DRM condition involves live presentation of word lists, worksheets, individualized feedback, and motivational instruction, whereas other conditions primarily involve passive podcast listening. This creates condition differences in experimenter contact, social evaluation, and arousal that could affect memory reports independently of the intended intervention.
issues.quote: “It will consist of the participants listening to experimenter presenting lists of words from a common category” / “At this moment in this group, the experimenter will give the following information to the participants”

issues.subcategory: hypothesis awareness assessment not prespecified for confirmatory use
issues.description: Participants are asked what they think the real purpose was, but the manuscript states only exploratory analysis and does not define coding, exclusion, or sensitivity analyses. Because several interventions reveal the deception and purpose, hypothesis awareness is central to interpretation and should be prespecified.
issues.quote: “Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.”

issues.subcategory: all critical-item exposure may not actually occur
issues.description: The design assumes collaborative recall exposes participants to misinformation, but the partner may not mention the discrepant detail, may agree with the participant, may guess, or both may fail to answer. Without ensuring or modeling actual exposure, the manipulation dose varies across items and dyads.
issues.quote: “If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.” / “However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, ‘white mug’ (such a situation can happen, e.g., as a result of the partner's guessing), the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading.”

issues.subcategory: conditional follow-up strategy may miss planned effects
issues.description: The hypotheses concern specific intervention-versus-control differences, but the plan makes follow-up comparisons conditional on a significant omnibus interaction. Omnibus-gated testing can be inefficient and may fail to test theoretically specified contrasts, especially when effects are concentrated in one intervention.
issues.quote: “The hypothesis concerning the efficacy of the methods for reducing the memory conformity effect will be verified by means of analyzing the interaction between the repeated measures factor of misinformation and the grouping factor.” / “In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.”

issues.subcategory: education intervention may alter confidence opposite to intended construct
issues.description: The Education intervention is intended to reduce conformity by teaching memory fallibility, but the manuscript acknowledges it could reduce confidence and increase suggestibility. Without measuring confidence/source monitoring and without separating education from warning or demand, the construct being manipulated is ambiguous.
issues.quote: “However, a caveat should be mentioned here: presenting participants with research confirming the fallibility of memory may result in decreased confidence in their own memory, which, in turn, might result in increased suggestibility.”

issues.subcategory: materials not sufficiently available for replication
issues.description: The exact podcast scripts, DRM word lists, motivational messages, control podcast content, final memory questions, and scoring keys are not provided. Approximate descriptions are insufficient because small wording differences in warnings, education, and motivation can substantially affect misinformation resistance.
issues.quote: “The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast about the fallibility of human memory.” / “The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast discussing the mechanisms of memory” / “The participants will also learn that a frequent source of erroneous testimonies is false information from the media or from other witnesses.”
